=== B4 (BLOCKING, and I can now say WHY, which no earlier record did). The
    required checks have not reported on this head — because a conflicted PR
    gets NO pull_request workflow runs at all. ===
Earlier reviewers recorded the symptom ("zero check runs on this head") as a
standalone mystery. It is not. It is a CONSEQUENCE of B1, and I measured the
causal link three ways:
  1. Timeline on THIS branch. Last pull_request CI run: 1fa35df, created
     2026-09-19T15:17:57Z. main then moved to de27f723 at 15:21:15Z and to
     bfe8507 at 15:27:21Z — four and ten minutes later. Every commit pushed
     after that (746d122 16:41Z, 4305428 17:34Z, bbdfccf 18:33Z, 5a0cea6
     18:36Z) produced ZERO workflow runs. REST commits/5a0cea62/check-runs
     -> total_count 0.
  2. A second conflicted PR behaves identically. #29 (cloud/runbook) is also
     mergeable=false; its last pull_request CI run is at 8d75890b,
     14:14:59Z, and NINE commits have landed since with only push-event
     lwb-auto-queue runs. Same shape, different PR.
  3. A CONTROL, which is what makes this more than correlation. PR #38 is
     mergeable=true. I pushed a review-record commit to it myself earlier in
     this same run, from this same container, with the same credentials:
     4d667eb got 19 check runs, CI and Handoff both triggered on
     pull_request. So reviewer pushes DO trigger CI. The variable that
     differs is the merge conflict, not who pushed.
The mechanism is GitHub's: a pull_request event needs refs/pull/N/merge, and
that ref cannot be built for a conflicted PR, so the workflows never start.
CONSEQUENCE, which is the part worth acting on: for this repository's merge
gate, a PR that conflicts with main can never go green — not "is red", but
its required contexts never report at all. Waiting for CI on a conflicted PR
is an infinite wait. B1 must be cleared FIRST; nothing else on this branch
can be evidenced until it is.

=== B5 (BLOCKING, NEW SINCE THE LAST REVIEW, AND UNREPAIRABLE IN PLACE).
    A private domain is in this branch's history and cannot be removed. ===
Commit bbdfccf (a reviewer's record commit) added a line quoting the offending
commit author with the local part elided but THE DOMAIN INTACT. Commit
5a0cea6 redacts it from the working tree and discloses it in an addendum —
which is the right thing to do and I credit it. It does not fix the gate:
    working-tree scan, needle = that domain -> lwb-env-leak check passed
    range scan f9b4dea..HEAD, same needle   -> FAIL: bbdfccfcdb81
                                               reviews/32/cloud-reviewer-c.json:10
    EXIT 1
CI's lwb-env-leak-history step reads every line ADDED by the PR's commits, so
it will stay red as long as bbdfccf is in the history. Force-push is denied.
The branch is therefore in the same unrepairable state that forced the re-cuts
of #30, #35 and #37. I confirmed by enumeration that bbdfccf is the ONLY
commit in the range that added it.
I cannot read the real LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES secret, so I cannot prove that
needle set contains this domain. Two things make that immaterial: PR #38
exists precisely because CI's real lwb-env-leak went red on the same class of
content, and removing a private address from a PUBLIC repository does not
need proof of a gate first.
A METHOD NOTE AGAINST MYSELF, because it nearly cost me this finding. My
first scan for leaked addresses was a regex for email-shaped strings
(`@domain.tld`) across added lines. It returned only allow-listed domains and
I briefly concluded the branch was clean. It was not: the leaked text has the
local part replaced by literal dots, so there is no "@" and an email regex
cannot see it. I caught it only by diffing the redaction commit. Anyone
auditing this class of leak with an address regex will get a false clean
result. (I re-checked PR #38 for the same blind spot: there I had ALSO run a
direct bare-domain needle grep over the full range, which returned zero, so
that AGREE does not rest on the flawed method.)
